name: OpenAI
statusNote: Still private as of Oct 2026. Confidentially filed IPO prospectus in June 2026; Altman ruled out a 2026 listing, IPO expected 2027. In early talks for a ~$30B pre-IPO round at ~$1.4T pre-money (no term sheet as of early Oct 2026).
oneLiner: Maker of ChatGPT, GPT-series frontier models, Codex and the OpenAI API platform.
founders: Sam Altman, Greg Brockman, Ilya Sutskever (left 2024 to found SSI), Wojciech Zaremba, John Schulman (left), Andrej Karpathy (left), Elon Musk and others.
talentSignals: Re-hired Thinking Machines co-founders Barret Zoph and Luke Metz plus Sam Schoenholz in Jan 2026, and Lilian Weng returned in Jul 2026 (https://techfundingnews.com/thinking-machines-in-talks-for-1b-at-40b-valuation-as-mira-muratis-ai-lab-races-ahead/)
Long history of alumni founding top labs (Anthropic, SSI, Thinking Machines, TypeSafe), which is both a talent signal and an attrition risk

rounds.leads: MGX among UAE funds in talks (reported)

research: Frontier research output: GPT-5.x series (GPT-5.4 referenced in Mar 2026), reasoning models (o-series), Codex, plus a steady stream of research papers and system cards. A 'GPT-6 Astra' launch is referenced in Reuters coverage.
traction: As of Mar 2026, OpenAI said it was making $2B revenue/month, enterprise was >40% of revenue, the API processed >15B tokens/min, and Codex had >2M weekly users (https://openai.com/index/accelerating-the-next-phase-ai/). Annualized revenue was ~$50B at end-Sep 2026, targeting >=$70B by year-end; Q3 run-rate growth was 77% total and 107% enterprise (https://www.cnbc.com/2026/10/08/open-ai-revenue-nvidia-oracle-coreweave.html). The widely reported $68B figure included partner gross revenue.
compute: Massive multi-cloud and Stargate commitments (Oracle and others). Oracle is a major compute supplier.
moat: ChatGPT consumer distribution (approaching 1B WAU), brand, capital access, and compute scale.
risks: Enormous compute obligations; Anthropic competing hard on enterprise and coding; revenue-metric confusion ($68B vs $50B) hit AI stocks; governance and safety controversies; IPO delayed to 2027.
notes: The Mar 2026 ARR of ~$24B is derived from the '$2B revenue per month' statement (x12), not quoted directly. Headcount not found. No individual X posts verified for this entry.

name: Anthropic
statusNote: Still private as of Oct 2026. Confidentially submitted a draft S-1 on 2026-06-01. No public S-1 on EDGAR as of early Oct. Bloomberg reports marketing could start the week of Nov 9 with listing before Thanksgiving at ~$2T (unconfirmed by the company).
oneLiner: Safety-focused frontier lab behind the Claude models and Claude Code; market leader in enterprise AI and coding.
founders: Dario Amodei (CEO, ex-OpenAI VP Research), Daniela Amodei, Jared Kaplan, Sam McCandlish, Tom Brown, Chris Olah, Jack Clark, Ben Mann and others (mostly ex-OpenAI).
talentSignals: Founding team authored GPT-3 and the scaling-laws papers; leader in interpretability research
Its alumni found new labs, e.g. Andi Peng co-founded Humans& (https://techcrunch.com/2026/01/20/humans-a-human-centric-ai-startup-founded-by-anthropic-xai-google-alums-raised-480m-seed-round/)
research: Frontier research: Claude model family, leading interpretability and alignment publications, and a Responsible Scaling Policy. The S-1 reportedly devotes ~80 of 261 pages to risk factors.
xPresence: @AnthropicAI 1.78M followers; @DarioAmodei 842k followers (fxtwitter, 2026-10-09). Staff (Claude Code team and others) are highly active and frequently viral.
traction: Run-rate went from ~$9B at end-2025 to $14B (Feb 2026), $47B (May) and >$65B (end-July) (Reuters). 2025 revenue was ~$4.6B, Q1 2026 $4.73B, and Q2 2026 >$11.5B preliminary (https://www.morningstar.com/stocks/anthropics-leaked-financials-reflect-fast-growth-not-2-trillion-valuation). Claude Code run-rate was >$2.5B as of Feb 2026 (Series G post).
compute: $518B of cloud, compute and infrastructure obligations (S-1 via Reuters). Contract to pay SpaceX/xAI $1.25B/month for Colossus compute (https://pitchbook.com/news/articles/financials-look-reckless-lifting-the-xai-hood-in-the-spacex-ipo).
moat: Enterprise and coding leadership (Claude Code), deep compute contracts, and safety brand trusted by regulated enterprises.
risks: Net loss of $42B in 2025 (S-1 via Reuters); huge compute commitments; ~$2T IPO valuation expectations; competition from OpenAI's coding push.
notes: Revenue run-rate after July not found from a primary source. Headcount not found. No individual X posts verified for this entry.

name: SpaceXAI (formerly xAI; includes X / Twitter)
statusNote: Two mergers, then an IPO. (1) xAI acquired X Corp in an all-stock deal on 2025-03-28 (X at $33B, xAI at $80B). (2) SpaceX acquired xAI (including X) via an all-stock triangular merger closing 2026-02-02 (xAI at $250B, SpaceX at $1T); xAI became a wholly owned subsidiary. (3) SpaceX IPO'd on Nasdaq Global Select and Nasdaq Texas under ticker SPCX: trading began 2026-06-12 at a $135 IPO price, closed 2026-06-15, ~$85.7B gross proceeds. (4) xAI rebranded to SpaceXAI on 2026-07-06 (@xai handle became @SpaceXAI). It is now the AI segment of public SpaceX (market cap ~$2.12T on 2026-10-09). NOT a private startup.
hq: Palo Alto / Memphis (Colossus); parent SpaceX in Starbase, Texas
oneLiner: Grok models plus the X social platform plus AI compute infrastructure (Colossus), now the AI segment of publicly listed SpaceX.
founders: Elon Musk with founding team incl. Igor Babuschkin (left 2025), Yuhuai (Tony) Wu, Christian Szegedy, Jimmy Ba, Greg Yang and others (ex-DeepMind, Google, OpenAI).
talentSignals: Heavy attrition: many co-founders have left. Ex-xAI researchers Eric Zelikman and Yuchen He co-founded Humans& (https://techcrunch.com/2026/01/20/humans-a-human-centric-ai-startup-founded-by-anthropic-xai-google-alums-raised-480m-seed-round/)
Musk said in Mar 2026 that Grok needed to be 'rebuilt from the foundations up', and SpaceX moved to buy Cursor (https://gizmodo.com/xai-is-dead-long-live-spacexai-2000782034)
research: Grok model series; Grok 4.5 launched 2026-07-08 on a new 'V9-Medium' 1.5T-parameter foundation model (https://x.ai/news/grok-4-5). Some open-weight releases of older Grok models. Limited academic publication output.
xPresence: @elonmusk 241.5M followers; @SpaceXAI (formerly @xai) 2.07M followers (fxtwitter, 2026-10-09). Owns the X platform itself.
traction: AI segment revenue: $3.2B in 2025, $818M in Q1 2026 and $2.56B in Q2 2026 (+247% YoY), of which $2.19B was AI Solutions & Infrastructure (compute rental) and $367M advertising. First positive segment adjusted EBITDA ($1.1B) in Q2, but an operating loss of ~$1.3B (https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/08/spacex-built-an-ai-business-its-best-customers-are-groks-competitors/). Grok ranked 5th of 7 assistants by web visits (May 2026 Similarweb data, same source).
compute: Colossus (1.4 GW, targeting >2 GW by end-2026 per the same 24/7 Wall St. article). Rents compute to Anthropic ($1.25B/month) and Google (~110k Nvidia GPUs, $920M/month at full capacity). AI capex was $15.8B in Q2 2026.
moat: Huge compute fleet, X distribution and data, and the SpaceX balance sheet and public-market access.
risks: Grok losing share; revenue increasingly comes from renting compute to rivals (terminable on 90 days' notice); talent attrition; Musk key-person and governance risk.
notes: EXCLUDE from the private-startup ranking: part of public SpaceX (SPCX). 'arr' holds Q2 2026 quarterly AI-segment revenue (not annualized); kind is approximated as FY revenue because the schema has no 'quarterly revenue' option. The user-listed 'X' (X Corp/Twitter) is the same entity. Market cap of $2.12T is for all of SpaceX, not the AI segment.

name: Safe Superintelligence (SSI)
statusNote: Still private as of Oct 2026. Nvidia made a strategic investment in Jul 2026 (reported as $5B).
oneLiner: 'Straight-shot' superintelligence lab with one goal and one product, pursuing a new (undisclosed) research direction.
founders: Ilya Sutskever (CEO; OpenAI co-founder and ex-chief scientist; AlexNet, seq2seq, GPT, o1), Daniel Levy (President, ex-OpenAI). Co-founder Daniel Gross left in 2025.
talentSignals: Led by Ilya Sutskever, one of the most cited researchers in deep learning (https://investor.nvidia.com/news/press-release-details/2026/Ilya-Sutskevers-Safe-Superintelligence-Inc--and-NVIDIA-Announce-Long-Term-Strategic-Partnership/default.aspx)
Co-founder/CEO Daniel Gross departed in 2025 (reportedly to Meta); Sutskever became CEO and said SSI rebuffed acquisition interest (https://texxr.com/handle/ilyasut)

rounds.leads: a16z, Sequoia, DST, NFDG, SV Angel

research: No public papers, models or products. The research direction is closely guarded; Nvidia says it obtained 'rare access' to it before investing.

xPosts.author: ssi
xPosts.summary: Announces long-term Nvidia partnership; Nvidia's 'substantial investment' will let SSI 10x compute in 12 months; 'our research is worth scaling'.

xPresence: @ilyasut 927k followers; @ssi 133k followers (fxtwitter, 2026-10-09). Posts rarely, but each post gets millions of views.
compute: Nvidia Vera Rubin access via the Jul 2026 partnership, expanding compute by an order of magnitude. Previously used Google Cloud TPUs (reported 2025).
moat: Sutskever's reputation, Nvidia compute partnership, and secrecy.
risks: No product or revenue; opaque research bet; departure of co-founder Gross; valuation not re-marked publicly since 2025.
notes: Post-money valuation after the Nvidia investment was not disclosed in primary sources. Multiples.vc lists ~$32B, which I could not confirm in Bloomberg/Reuters. The Feb/Apr 2025 date for the $32B round varies by source. Headcount not found.

name: Thinking Machines Lab
statusNote: Still private as of Oct 2026. In talks (not closed) to raise $5-6B at >=$40B pre-money, with Accel leading and Nvidia ~half.
oneLiner: Frontier lab building customizable open-weight models (Inkling family) and the Tinker fine-tuning platform.
founders: Mira Murati (CEO, ex-OpenAI CTO); co-founders included Barret Zoph, Luke Metz, Lilian Weng (all since returned to OpenAI) and John Schulman (OpenAI co-founder; listed in Jul 2026 as Thinking Machines angel in Prime Intellect's round).
talentSignals: Launched with ~two dozen OpenAI veterans; the $2B seed was largely a pedigree bet (https://techfundingnews.com/thinking-machines-in-talks-for-1b-at-40b-valuation-as-mira-muratis-ai-lab-races-ahead/)
Heavy attrition: CTO Barret Zoph, Luke Metz and Sam Schoenholz returned to OpenAI in Jan 2026, and Lilian Weng left for OpenAI in Jul 2026 (same source)
Murati holds board voting control on major decisions (https://thenextweb.com/news/thinking-machines-lab-6bn-round-nvidia-accel)
research: Inkling (released 2026-07-15) is an open-weights 975B-total/41B-active multimodal MoE (text, image, audio; up to 1M context; 45T training tokens). Inkling-Small (276B/12B active) followed 2026-07-30. Tinker fine-tuning API and 'Connectionism' research blog posts.

xPosts.author: thinkymachines
xPosts.summary: Introduces Inkling, an open-weights multimodal reasoning model, available for fine-tuning on Tinker.

xPresence: @miramurati 1.03M followers; @thinkymachines 184k followers (fxtwitter, 2026-10-09). Launch posts get millions of views.
traction: Run-rate over $100M per a TechCrunch source; The Information reports 'hundreds of millions'. Revenue comes from Tinker usage-based fine-tuning and compute fees.
compute: Multiyear Nvidia chip supply deal (Mar 2026) and Google Cloud partnership (https://valueaddvc.com/blog/thinking-machines-valuation-what-mira-muratis-ai-lab-is-worth-and-who-funded-it). Inkling-Small trained on GB300 NVL72.
moat: Open-weights model plus fine-tuning platform; Nvidia backing.
risks: Co-founder attrition to OpenAI; $50B round collapsed in Jan 2026; very high revenue multiple; Inkling admitted 'not the strongest' model.
notes: Exact round size is disputed ($1B per TechCrunch vs $5-6B per The Information's update). Headcount not found.

name: Mistral AI
statusNote: Still private as of Oct 2026. The CFO said an IPO remains a possibility.
oneLiner: European frontier lab building open-weight and commercial models plus sovereign AI infrastructure and enterprise products (Le Chat, Mistral Compute).
founders: Arthur Mensch (CEO, ex-DeepMind), Guillaume Lample (ex-FAIR, LLaMA), Timothée Lacroix (ex-FAIR).
talentSignals: Founders are LLaMA (FAIR) and DeepMind alumni
Largest equity round ever for a European tech company (https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/08/mistral-raises-e3b-as-sovereign-ai-becomes-big-business/)

rounds.leads: Samsung Electronics; co-leads Scaleup Europe Fund (EQT), PSG Equity

research: Prolific open-weight releases (Mistral 7B, Mixtral, Mistral Large/Medium/Small, Codestral, Magistral, Devstral). Widely used open models; technical reports.
xPresence: @MistralAI 222k followers; @arthurmensch 88k followers (fxtwitter, 2026-10-09). Model drops (historically magnet links) frequently go viral.
traction: ARR slightly above $1B as of Sep 2026 per the CFO (WSJ), up from ~$400M a year earlier. Benefiting from sovereign-AI demand in Europe.
compute: Building its own compute (Mistral Compute); Nvidia is an investor.
moat: European sovereign-AI positioning, government and industrial partnerships (ASML, Samsung), and open-weight ecosystem.
risks: Models trail US/Chinese frontier; much smaller capital base than US labs.
notes: Series C was EUR 1.7B at EUR 11.7B post; USD figures in the rounds list are approximate conversions. The $400M 2025 revenue figure comes from Multiples.vc (secondary). Headcount not found. No individual X posts verified for this entry.

name: Cohere
statusNote: Private as of Oct 2026. Signed a definitive agreement on 2026-09-16 to combine with Germany's Aleph Alpha (Cohere is the surviving brand/acquirer; pending regulatory approval). In advanced talks (Sep 2026) to raise $2-3B at ~$20B. No IPO filing.
oneLiner: Enterprise and sovereign AI models (Command, Embed, Rerank) and the North agent platform for regulated industries and governments.
founders: Aidan Gomez (CEO, Transformer paper co-author, ex-Google Brain), Nick Frosst (ex-Google Brain), Ivan Zhang.
talentSignals: CEO Aidan Gomez co-authored 'Attention Is All You Need'
Aleph Alpha co-CEO Ilhan Scheer becomes COO of the combined company (https://www.reuters.com/legal/transactional/cohere-aleph-alpha-combine-target-enterprise-ai-market-2026-09-16/)

rounds.stage: Series E (Schwarz Group lead commitment, structured)

research: Cohere Labs (formerly Cohere For AI) publishes regularly: the Aya multilingual open models and papers at major venues. Open-weight Command R/A releases. Aleph Alpha's Heidelberg office becomes a research hub.
traction: ~$240M ARR in 2025 (beat $200M target), >50% QoQ growth through 2025, ~70% gross margins (CNBC). Compute deals: Bell 7MW BC data centre (US$220M), STACKIT, 50MW from Humain (https://thelogic.co/news/cohere-aleph-alpha-deal-terms-agreed/).
compute: Schwarz Group's STACKIT (up to EUR 13B compute investment), Bell Canada, Humain (Saudi), Nvidia/AMD as investors.
moat: Sovereign/regulated-industry positioning in Canada and Germany with government backing.
risks: Models behind the frontier; merger-integration risk; small revenue vs US labs.
notes: The ~$20B valuation is tied to the merged entity (first disclosed Apr 2026) and the pending round; it is not a closed priced round. 2026 ARR not found. Headcount not found. No individual X posts verified for this entry.

name: Reflection AI
statusNote: Still private as of Oct 2026. CEO confirmed on CNBC raising at a $25B valuation; PitchBook lists a $2.5B Series C completed 2026-04-23.
oneLiner: US 'open frontier' lab building open-weight models (Beam) and sovereign AI systems for governments and enterprises; positioned as America's answer to DeepSeek.
founders: Misha Laskin (CEO, ex-DeepMind, Gemini RL/reward modeling) and Ioannis Antonoglou (ex-DeepMind, AlphaGo/AlphaZero/MuZero co-creator).
talentSignals: Founders are ex-DeepMind (AlphaGo, Gemini) researchers (https://www.reuters.com/business/nvidia-backed-reflection-ai-raises-2-billion-funding-boosts-valuation-8-billion-2025-10-09/)
Team of ~200 per PitchBook, ~320 per Multiples (2026)
research: Beam (announced 2026-10-05) is a 501B-total/23B-active sparse MoE open-weight model, trained from scratch, with Apache 2.0 weights promised for Oct 2026 (not yet on Hugging Face as of Oct 8). Earlier product: Asimov code-research agent.

xPosts.author: reflection_ai
xPosts.summary: Introduces Beam, a 501B/23B-active agentic open model trained from scratch; full weights promised this month.

traction: Early revenue (PitchBook: 'Generating Revenue'). JV with Shinsegae Group (Mar 2026, per PitchBook). Revenue figures not found.
compute: Nvidia-backed. Reportedly signed a SpaceX compute agreement worth up to $6.3B in Jun 2026 (Multiples.vc; unverified in primary reporting).
moat: US-government-aligned open-weight positioning and large capital base.
risks: First major model not yet fully released; own benchmarks show it trailing GLM/DeepSeek on several evals; ~$27.5B valuation on little revenue.
notes: The $25B is pre-money (WSJ), so $27.5B post is implied. Round closing is confirmed by PitchBook and the CEO on CNBC, but the lead investor is only reported. Headcount sources conflict (200 vs ~320).

name: Poolside
statusNote: Private as of Oct 2026, but Aug 2026 Nvidia deal: $6B non-exclusive license of Poolside's model factory, job offers to ~109 employees, plus a $1B investment at $12B pre-money. Founders remain and Poolside stays independent (quasi acqui-hire / license structure).
oneLiner: Builds foundation models for software development (Malibu, Point) trained with reinforcement learning from code execution feedback.
founders: Jason Warner (co-CEO, ex-GitHub CTO) and Eiso Kant (co-CEO, ex-source{d}).
talentSignals: ~109 employees received offers to join Nvidia as part of the license deal, likely hollowing out the team (https://runtimewire.com/article/nvidia-pays-6b-to-license-poolside-s-factory-for-u-s-open-weight-models)
Reportedly failed to close a $2B round in spring 2026 (https://www.forbes.com/sites/jonmarkman/2026/08/24/nvidia-pays-poolside-6b-to-license-its-model-factory-and-109-workers/)
research: RLCEF (reinforcement learning from code execution feedback); Malibu and Point models; limited public papers.
traction: Enterprise and defense-focused coding models. Revenue estimate ~$50M (Latka via Value Add, weak source). $6B license fee to be distributed to investors by end-2027.
compute: Previously a 10k-GPU cluster (2024 blog); compute access reportedly squeezed before the Nvidia deal.
moat: Weak: core technology now non-exclusively licensed to Nvidia and much of the team offered Nvidia jobs.
risks: Team hollowing; competition from frontier-lab coding agents; unclear go-forward strategy.
notes: The 2024 Series B valuation is reported as $3B by some outlets and $2B by Value Add. The $13B post-money is implied from $12B pre + $1B. Revenue and headcount are from weak secondary sources. No individual X posts verified for this entry.

name: AMI Labs
statusNote: Private; raised a $1.03B seed in Mar 2026. Confirmed as Yann LeCun's startup (the @amilabs X account and the amilabs.xyz domain belong to it).
oneLiner: Builds world-model AI systems (JEPA-style) that understand the physical world, with persistent memory, reasoning and planning, as an alternative to LLMs.
founders: Yann LeCun (Executive Chairman; Turing Award, FAIR founder, ex-Meta chief AI scientist); CEO Alex LeBrun (ex-Nabla, Wit.ai).
talentSignals: Chief Science Officer Saining Xie, Chief Research & Innovation Officer Pascale Fung, VP World Models Michael Rabbat (ex-FAIR), COO Laurent Solly (ex-Meta VP Europe) (https://techcrunch.com/2026/03/09/yann-lecuns-ami-labs-raises-1-03-billion-to-build-world-models/)
Only 12 employees at the time of the seed (https://www.nytimes.com/2026/03/10/technology/ami-labs-yann-lecun-funding.html)

rounds.leads: Cathay Innovation, Greycroft, Hiro Capital, HV Capital, Bezos Expeditions

research: Founding team built JEPA/V-JEPA and much of FAIR's self-supervised learning work. No AMI-branded publications or models found yet.
compute: Nvidia, Samsung and Toyota are among investors; no specific compute deal found.
moat: LeCun's brand and contrarian world-model thesis; European champion status.
risks: Unproven paradigm; small early team; no product timeline.
notes: $3.5B is pre-money, so $4.53B post is implied. LeCun's announcement tweet was quoted by Techloy (2026-03-10), but I did not find its status ID, so it is not listed. Founding date late 2025 (LeCun left Meta end-2025).

name: Humans&
oneLiner: 'Human-centric frontier AI lab' building models for collaboration and coordination among people; first release is Persimmon, a user-simulation model.
founders: Eric Zelikman (CEO; STaR/Quiet-STaR author, Stanford PhD, led Grok 2 post-training and Grok 4 agent RL at xAI), Andi Peng (ex-Anthropic RL/post-training on Claude 3.5-4.5), Georges Harik (Google employee #7), Yuchen He (ex-xAI), Noah Goodman (Stanford professor).
talentSignals: Founders from xAI, Anthropic, Google and Stanford (https://techcrunch.com/2026/01/20/humans-a-human-centric-ai-startup-founded-by-anthropic-xai-google-alums-raised-480m-seed-round/)
Zelikman led Grok 2 post-training and the Grok 4 agent RL recipe (https://www.scalevp.com/blog/announcing-our-investment-in-humans)
Angels include Igor Babuschkin, Tony Wu, Thomas Wolf and Logan Kilpatrick (https://humansand.ai/about)
research: Persimmon v0.1 (2026-09-10) is a research-preview user model post-trained on Nvidia Nemotron-3-Ultra 550B-A55B, with playground, API and new evals (Turing test, Trickle Test).
traction: Research preview only (Persimmon playground/API with gated access). No revenue reported.
risks: Vague product direction; first model is a post-train on Nvidia's base model rather than from-scratch pretraining.
notes: Headcount not found. The launch tweet status ID was not found, so no X posts are verified.

name: Sakana AI
statusNote: Private as of Oct 2026; Series B final close Apr 2026.
oneLiner: Tokyo lab pursuing nature-inspired AI (evolutionary model merging, AI Scientist, self-improvement), selling to Japanese enterprises and government.
founders: David Ha (CEO, ex-Google Brain Tokyo, ex-Stability), Llion Jones (CTO, Transformer paper co-author), Ren Ito (COO, ex-Mercari, ex-Japanese MOFA).
talentSignals: Founder Llion Jones co-authored 'Attention Is All You Need'; David Ha is a well-known Google Brain researcher
Strategic investors include Google, Citi, Mitsubishi Electric and In-Q-Tel (https://metallab.ai/en/2026/8/inside-sakana-ai-japans-most-valuable-ai-startup)
research: Strong research output: The AI Scientist, evolutionary model merging, Transformer², continuous thought machines, and many papers at ICLR/NeurIPS-class venues. 2026 products: Fugu, Marlin (first commercial product, Jun 2026), Sakana Chat.
xPresence: @hardmaru (David Ha) 441k followers; @SakanaAILabs 141k followers (fxtwitter, 2026-10-09). Research posts regularly go viral.
traction: Enterprise deals with Japanese banks (MUFG and others). Revenue not disclosed; a ~$30M figure circulating is an unconfirmed third-party estimate. The CEO has said no proven profitable GenAI business model exists yet.
compute: Nvidia collaboration (Series A); Google strategic partnership (Jan 2026).
moat: Japan national-champion status and deep corporate/government relationships.
risks: Small capital base vs frontier labs; commercialization early; past controversy over overstated research claims (AI CUDA Engineer, 2025).
notes: Series B amounts are in yen: JPY 32B total (~$200M) at ~JPY 432B (~$2.7B). The Series A valuation of $1.5B is 'reported'. Revenue not found. No individual X posts verified for this entry.

name: Liquid AI
statusNote: Private; no new primary round disclosed since the Dec 2024 Series A (as of Aug-Oct 2026).
oneLiner: MIT CSAIL spinout building non-transformer Liquid Foundation Models (LFM2/LFM2.5) optimized for on-device and edge deployment.
founders: Ramin Hasani (CEO), Mathias Lechner (CTO), Alexander Amini (CSO), Daniela Rus (MIT CSAIL director).
talentSignals: Founders invented liquid time-constant networks at MIT CSAIL under Daniela Rus (https://hokai.io/hub/companies/liquid-ai)
research: Open-weight LFM2 family (text, vision, audio, 8.3B MoE) in 2025, then LFM2.5 in 2026 (including a 3B vision model in Sep 2026). Claimed 52 models and 38M+ Hugging Face downloads (https://hokai.io/hub/companies/liquid-ai). Peer-reviewed liquid-network papers.
traction: Mercedes-Benz on-device partnership (Apr 2026, production in 2H 2026) (https://www.linkedin.com/posts/raminhasani_im-proud-to-announce-our-new-partnership-activity-7453096470251208704-7rQ0). MacPaw partnership (Aug 2026); Shopify and AMD relationships (Bloomberg Tech Disruptors, Sep 2026). Revenue not disclosed.
moat: Architecture IP for efficient edge inference; OEM partnerships.
risks: No disclosed raise in ~22 months; a secondary print of ~$1.6B (Jun 2026, QuantLogix) suggests a markdown; edge models face competition from Google/Meta/Qwen small models.
notes: Series A valuation was not officially published; Bloomberg said 'more than $2B', and data providers say $2.28-2.4B. Revenue not found. No individual X posts verified for this entry.

name: Prime Intellect
statusNote: Private; $130M Series A at $1B valuation in Jul 2026.
oneLiner: 'Open superintelligence stack': compute marketplace, decentralized and RL training infrastructure (prime-rl, verifiers, Environments Hub), and open models (INTELLECT series) for enterprises to train their own models and agents.
talentSignals: Founder-heavy angel list including John Schulman, Dwarkesh Patel, Aravind Srinivas, Aaron Levie and Asher Spector (Flapping Airplanes) (https://x.com/PrimeIntellect/status/2074899489190785419)
Small team (~40-50 employees per LinkedIn data in a Jul 2026 post) shipping 100B+ models
research: INTELLECT-1/2 (decentralized training) and INTELLECT-3 (106B/12B-active MoE, RL on 512 H200s, open weights, arXiv 2512.16144). Open-source prime-rl, verifiers and Environments Hub. Very strong OSS research output for its size.

xPosts.author: PrimeIntellect
xPosts.summary: Announces $130M Series A led by Radical Ventures with NVIDIA, Intel Capital and Dell to build the Open Superintelligence Stack.

xPresence: @PrimeIntellect 85.8k followers; @vincentweisser 32.7k followers (fxtwitter, 2026-10-09). Staff such as Will Brown are well-known RL posters (handle not verified).
traction: Enterprise customers such as Ramp, which built a model beating Claude Opus 4.6 on some spreadsheet tasks (SiliconANGLE). Revenue not disclosed.
compute: Aggregated compute marketplace; Nvidia, Intel and Dell as investors.
moat: Open-source RL ecosystem mindshare (verifiers / Environments Hub); otherwise modest.
risks: Compute marketplace is commoditized; competition from Thinking Machines' Tinker and the hyperscalers.

name: TypeSafe AI
statusNote: Private; came out of stealth 2026-09-15 with a $40M seed led by DCVC. Not related to the old Scala/Akka company Typesafe Inc. (now Lightbend).
oneLiner: Builds 'System One Models': non-chat models (first model: Jev) that return typed, calibrated-probability decisions that software can act on, trained with RL for Calibrated Decisions (RLCD).
founders: Diogo Almeida (CEO; OpenAI MTS 2020-2024, InstructGPT and GPT-4 tech report co-author, company bills him as RLHF co-inventor; ex-Google Brain), Sasha Sheng (COO; ex-Meta/FAIR research engineer, NeurIPS/ECCV author), Erik Gafni (CTO; repeat founder of Ravel, early at Invitae and Freenome).
talentSignals: CEO co-authored InstructGPT, the research behind ChatGPT (https://typesafe.ai/team)
Team from OpenAI, Google Brain, Meta/FAIR, Stripe, Airbnb, Plaid and Docker (https://typesafe.ai/team)
a16z's Martin Casado and Ben Horowitz publicly championed Jev (a16z podcast/X, Sep 2026, via https://twiscan.com/en/x/CompleteSkeptic)
research: New architecture plus parallel sampler plus RLCD training method. Jev claims similar intelligence to LLMs on 'System One' tasks at ~100x speed/efficiency, priced at $42 per billion input tokens with free output. No peer-reviewed papers found.

xPosts.author: CompleteSkeptic

xPresence: @typesafeai 165k followers (account joined Jan 2026); CEO @CompleteSkeptic ~151k followers (twstalker/twiscan; fxtwitter profile lookup failed); @EGafni 8k; @hackgoofer (Sasha Sheng) 9.1k; @notkevinzhang 6.3k (fxtwitter, 2026-10-09). The launch went strongly viral (3.2M views).
traction: Launched 2026-09-15 in early access, open to all 2026-09-20; capacity constraints forced temporary signup pauses and removal of free credits (CEO posts, Sep 27). CopilotKit integration. The CEO's claim of 'a quarter of the Fortune 500 onboarded' is an unverified self-claim.
moat: Novel model class plus first-mover in typed-decision APIs; easily copied if frontier labs offer cheap classification endpoints.
risks: Narrow use case (classification/decisions); tiny seed vs frontier labs; capacity constraints; claims not independently benchmarked.
notes: The $40M seed amount and DCVC lead come from the CEO's LinkedIn post (primary but self-published); no press coverage found. Founding date: CEO role from Jan 2024, domain registered May 2024 (https://hraness.com/typesafe/history, weak source). Valuation and headcount not found. The 165k-follower account joined 2026-01-23 per fxtwitter; the follower count is unusually high for a pre-launch lab (organic growth not verified).

name: Flapping Airplanes
oneLiner: Foundational AI research lab pursuing radically more data-efficient learning (targets 100,000x-1,000,000x sample-efficiency gains); not currently commercializing.
founders: Ben Spector (founder of Prod incubator, behind Cursor, Mercor, Etched and Decart; MIT; Stanford PhD under Chris Ré), Asher Spector (Stanford Statistics PhD, former North American debate champion), Aidan Smith (Thiel Fellow, 3 years at Neuralink).
talentSignals: Team includes IMO/IOI/IPhO medalists; advisors and angels include Chris Ré, Andrej Karpathy and Jeff Dean (https://flappingairplanes.com/)
Sequoia's David Cahn calls it the 'young person's AGI lab', betting on raw talent over brand-name hires (https://sequoiacap.com/article/partnering-with-flapping-airplanes/)
Ben Spector's Prod network spawned companies with >$50B combined valuation (https://www.gv.com/news/why-we-invested-in-flapping-airplanes)
research: No publications or models found yet; research directions include rethinking loss functions and gradient descent.
